tool_args.rationale: All five paid rows have H ≤ 0.48, while the forecast target is H = 23.3. The slow-horizon probe can distinguish amplitude and time-scale combinations that agree in the pilot window but predict different long-horizon gains, including a possible sign reversal.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the five-parameter sink-coupled model now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: At short horizons, slow adaptation depends mainly on the ratio of its amplitude to its time constant. Fitting the pilot rows does not establish the adaptation strength at H = 23.3.
It omits the observed sink-gradient signature and still leaves the slow time scale weakly constrained.
It costs slightly less but is not identified as testing the long-horizon behavior that drives forecast uncertainty.
The auxiliary measurement does not constrain slow adaptation.
